title: King Charles Sends a Letter About Harry and Meghan: Here's What It Says
summary:
Have you ever played a game where everyone has a role? In the royal family, some members are "working" royals — they do official duties for the Queen or King. Others are not. Prince Harry and his wife Meghan are not working royals, and King Charles III just sent a letter to make that super clear.

Why? Because Harry and Meghan recently came back to live in the UK. Some people were confused about their status. So the King's top official, the Lord Chamberlain, sent a letter to government and military leaders. It said that Harry and Meghan will keep not using their royal titles for official work. Any charity work they do will be private, not official.

This is important because Harry has been fighting to get back his police protection. When he and Meghan stopped being working royals in 2020, they lost their round-the-clock police guard. Harry wants that protection back, especially when he's in the UK with his family. But the decision is up to a special government group called RAVEC.

The letter also says that if any official group has questions about how to treat the Duke and Duchess (that's Harry and Meghan's fancy title), they should ask Buckingham Palace.

Some people think the King sent this letter because he's worried that Harry and Meghan might start acting like a "parallel royal court" — like a second royal family that competes with the real one. That could be confusing for everyone!

So now it's official: Harry and Meghan are still part of the family, but they're not working royals. And the King wants everyone to know it.
why_it_matters: This story shows that even a famous family needs clear roles and rules, and that disagreements about those rules can affect people's safety and sense of belonging.

background_read: The British royal family has a rule: some members are 'working royals' who do official duties for the King, while others are not.
Prince Harry (the King's younger son) and his wife Meghan stopped being working royals in 2020, and that meant they lost their round-the-clock police guard.
The Lord Chamberlain (the King's top official, who helps run royal ceremonies) sent the letter to make the family's rules clear.
Article_Structure: WHO: King Charles III, Prince Harry, Meghan, and the King's top official called the Lord Chamberlain.
WHAT: A letter was sent saying Harry and Meghan are still part of the family but are not working royals, so their charity work is private, not official.
WHERE: The United Kingdom, where Harry and Meghan recently returned to live.
WHY: People were confused about their royal role, and Harry also wants to get back his police protection.

perspectives.description: Making the rules clear helps government leaders, the military, and charities know exactly how to treat Harry and Meghan.
They may feel the letter pushes them further away from the official family. Harry also worries about keeping his family safe without police protection.
Because the royal family represents the U.K., people expect it to be clear about who is acting officially and who is acting privately.
